Check yourself: What does the Back button do?

Answer: It takes you to the page you looked at before the current one.

slides.title: Searching the Internet
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Chrome and go to www.google.com.
  2. Step 2: Type a question (e.g., “easy dinner recipes”).
  3. Step 3: Press Enter to see results.
  4. Step 4: Click a link to visit a website.
⭐ Activity: Search for a topic of interest online.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Open Chrome and click the address bar.
  2. Type easy dinner recipes and press Enter. (Typing www.google.com first also works.)
  3. Read the results. Each shows a title, a web address and a short description. Results marked Sponsored are adverts.
  4. Click one result to open it.
  5. Click the Back arrow and try another.

You should see a list of pages and be able to open them. Too many unrelated results? Add more words, such as easy dinner recipes with rice. If you mistype, Google may say "Showing results for" with the correct spelling.

Power-user layer
  • Use specific words. They give better results than long questions.
  • Put quotes around an exact phrase: "how to save a file".
  • Type site:bbc.com plus words to search only one website.
  • Use the tabs under the search box, such as Images or News.
  • On a page, press Ctrl+F to find a word.
  • Ctrl+click on a result to open it in a new tab and keep your results.
  • Check the date and source before you trust an answer.
Check yourself: Why should you add more specific words to a search?

Answer: Specific words give fewer but more relevant results, so you find your answer faster.

slides.title: Saving Favorite Websites
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Visit a website (e.g., www.bbc.com).
  2. Step 2: Click the star icon in the address bar.
  3. Step 3: Name the bookmark (e.g., “News”).
  4. Step 4: Click Bookmarks menu to reopen.
⭐ Activity: Bookmark a favorite site.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Open a website you like, for example a news site.
  2. Click the star icon at the right end of the address bar. (Ctrl+D does the same.)
  3. In the box, change the name to News. Keep Folder as Bookmarks bar. Click Done.
  4. To reopen it: press Ctrl+Shift+B to show the bookmarks bar, then click your bookmark. Or click the three dots, then Bookmarks and lists (the menu name differs in some versions), then choose it.

The star turns filled in. Cannot see the bookmark? The bar is hidden. Press Ctrl+Shift+B.

Power-user layer
  • Right-click the bookmarks bar and choose Add folder to group sites, such as Work and Learning.
  • Use short names so more fit on the bar.
  • Ctrl+Shift+O opens the bookmark manager, where you can tidy and delete.
  • To remove a bookmark, click the filled star and choose Remove.
  • Only sign in to Chrome to sync bookmarks on your own computer, never a shared one.
Check yourself: What shortcut bookmarks the page you are on?

Answer: Ctrl+D (or click the star in the address bar).

slides.title: Staying Safe Online
slides.content:
1. HTTPS: Look for “https://” in website addresses (secure).
  2. Avoid Suspicious Links: Don’t click unknown links.
  3. Strong Passwords: Use letters, numbers, symbols (e.g., Sunny2025!).
🔒 Discuss: Safe vs. unsafe websites.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Open gmail.com. Look at the left end of the address bar. There is a small icon. In recent Chrome versions it may look like a settings symbol, not a padlock.
  2. Click once in the address bar. The full address starts with https://. Chrome often hides this part until you click.
  3. Click the small icon. It should say the connection is secure.
  4. Now write one strong password idea in your notebook: three unrelated words, a number and a symbol. Do not use the lesson example or your birthday.

If Chrome says Not secure, do not type passwords or card details on that page.

Power-user layer
  • HTTPS means the connection is private. It does not prove the website is honest. Scam sites can use it too.
  • Use a different password for each important account, especially email.
  • Use 2-Step Verification where offered. A stolen password alone is then not enough.
  • Never share one-time codes or mobile money PINs with anyone.
  • Check the spelling of the address before you log in. Fake sites copy real names with small changes.
  • Install Windows updates.
Check yourself: Does https:// mean a website is honest?

Answer: No. It means your connection is encrypted, but scammers can use it too. Still check the address and never trust unexpected offers.

slides.title: Recognizing Phishing Emails
slides.content:
1. Phishing: Fake emails asking for personal info.
  2. Red Flags:
    1. Unknown sender (e.g., random123@email.com).
    2. Urgent demands (e.g., “Send money now!”).
    3. Strange links or attachments.
  3. Action: Delete or report as spam.
⭐ Activity: Look at an example of a fake email and discuss why it is dangerous.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Open the sample email. Do not click any link or attachment.
  2. Check the sender's address, not only the name. In Gmail, click the small arrow beside the sender to see it. Does it match the real organisation?
  3. Move the mouse over a link without clicking. The real destination shows at the bottom-left of the window. Does it match?
  4. Look for urgency, threats, prizes, spelling mistakes, and requests for a password or PIN.
  5. If it looks fake, click the three dots at the top-right of the message and choose Report phishing. Then delete it.

If you did click and typed a password, change it on the real website straight away.

Power-user layer
  • Check in another way. Call the organisation on a number you already know, or type its website yourself.
  • A genuine organisation should never ask for your password or PIN by email.
  • Be careful with unexpected attachments, especially zip files and programs.
  • The same tricks come by SMS and WhatsApp.
  • Tell friends and family when you see a new scam.
  • 2-Step Verification protects you if a password leaks.
Check yourself: An email says: "Your account closes in one hour. Click here and enter your password." What do you do?

Answer: Do not click. Urgency plus a password request is a phishing sign. Report phishing, delete it, and if worried go to the real website by typing its address.

slides.title: Safe Browsing Habits
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Check for “https://” before entering info.
  2. Step 2: Don’t share personal details (e.g., bank info).
  3. Step 3: Log out of websites (e.g., Gmail) when done.
⭐ Activity: Sign out of Gmail.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Before typing any information, check the address and the secure icon at the left of the address bar.
  2. Share only what is needed. Never send your PIN or password by email or message.
  3. When finished, sign out. In Gmail, click your profile picture and choose Sign out.
  4. Close the browser window with the X.
  5. On a shared computer, start with a private window: press Ctrl+Shift+N.

You should see the Gmail sign-in page when you return. Signing out of one site does not sign you out of others, so check each one. If Chrome offers to save a password on a shared computer, click Never.

Power-user layer
  • Press Windows+L to lock the screen when you step away.
  • On a shared computer clear history with Ctrl+Shift+Delete.
  • A private window only stops this computer from saving your history. It does not make you invisible to websites or the network.
  • Download programs only from the official website.
  • Avoid banking on public Wi-Fi.
  • Check privacy settings on social media.
Check yourself: What does Windows+L do, and why is it useful?

Answer: It locks the computer. This stops others from using your open accounts while you are away.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Open Chrome and search for “weather forecast.”
  2. Task 2: Bookmark a favorite website (e.g., a news site).
  3. Task 3: Review a sample email and identify if it’s phishing.
  4. Task 4: Sign out of Gmail and sign back in.
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!
Step-by-step layer
  1. Open Chrome. Click the address bar, type weather forecast and press Enter. Open a result and read today's forecast. Click Back.
  2. Open a news site. Press Ctrl+D, name it News, click Done. Press Ctrl+Shift+B and click your bookmark to test it.
  3. Open the sample email. Check the sender address, hover over the link, and look for urgency. Say aloud three reasons it is or is not phishing.
  4. Open Gmail. Click your profile picture, choose Sign out. Sign in again with your address and password.

Expected: you see the forecast, a working bookmark, a correct phishing decision and your Inbox. Stretch: create a bookmarks folder named Daily and drag your bookmark into it.

Power-user layer
  • Time yourself. Aim to do all four tasks without help.
  • Use shortcuts: Ctrl+L, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+Shift+B, Ctrl+T.
  • Turn the phishing check into a habit: sender, link, urgency, request.
  • Always sign out when you finish on a shared machine.
  • Repeat this walk-through at home until it feels easy.
Check yourself: After bookmarking a site, how can you open it quickly?

Answer: Press Ctrl+Shift+B to show the bookmarks bar and click it, or use the three dots menu and open Bookmarks.

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Find recipes, news, or tips online.
  2. Stay safe from scams and phishing.
  3. Prepare for advanced spreadsheets next week!
⏳ Note: Internet skills help in real life.
Step-by-step layer

Use the internet to earn and save.

  1. Pick a real need: prices of goods you sell, a job notice, or how to fill a form.
  2. Search with specific words. Open two or three results.
  3. Compare them. Prefer official or well-known sources.
  4. Press Ctrl+D to bookmark the best one.
  5. Create a Work folder on the bookmarks bar and put it there.
  6. Write five safety rules in your notebook, such as "never share my PIN".

You should now have a saved, trusted page. Not sure a source is real? Look for an official website and see if others agree.

Power-user layer
  • Internet skills open work. You can apply for jobs, find customers and suppliers, learn free skills and use government and bank services online.
  • One scam can wipe out savings, so safety protects your income.
  • Check a supplier before paying. Be careful of anyone who rushes you.
  • Keep records of online orders and payments.
  • Learn something new every week. Free tutorials exist for many trades.
Check yourself: Give an example of safe internet habits protecting your money.

Answer: Checking a supplier before paying, never sharing a PIN or password, and spotting a phishing email before clicking.

slides.title: Q&A and Homework
slides.content:
1. Ask: Any questions about browsing or safety?
  2. Homework:
    1. Search for a topic (e.g., “gardening tips”).
    2. Bookmark a website you like.
    3. Check your Gmail for suspicious emails.
  3. Next Week: Advanced spreadsheets!
❓ Encourage: Ask questions and use handouts for practice.
Step-by-step layer

Common beginner questions:

  1. Is public Wi-Fi safe? It is fine for reading the news. Avoid banking and typing important passwords on it.
  2. How do I know a website is real? Check the spelling of the address, look for https, and see if known sources link to it. Be careful with offers that seem too good.
  3. Does Google cost money? Searching is free, but you use your data bundle.
  4. I clicked a bad link. Close the tab. Do not type anything. If you did, change that password at once.

Homework: search, bookmark, then check your Gmail Spam folder.

Power-user layer
  • Do the homework on your own so the steps become automatic.
  • Open Spam and Promotions in Gmail and practise spotting red flags.
  • Add each new safety rule to your notebook.
  • Ask someone older or younger to show you a scam they have seen.
  • Write down any question for next class. There are no silly ones.
Check yourself: You clicked a link in a strange email and typed your password. What should you do?

Answer: Change the password on the real website straight away, turn on 2-Step Verification, and check the account for strange activity.

slides.title: Advanced Spreadsheets
slides.content:
1. Objective: Learn advanced spreadsheet skills.
  2. Today: Use formulas and charts in Excel.
  3. Why It Matters: Analyze budgets or plans easily!
  4. What numbers do you want to analyze? (e.g., monthly expenses)
Step-by-step layer
  1. Click Start, type Excel, press Enter.
  2. Click Blank workbook.
  3. Type Item in A1 and Amount in B1. Below, type Rent, Food, Transport in A2:A4, and any amounts in B2:B4.
  4. Click B5 and type =SUM(B2:B4). Press Enter.
  5. Press Ctrl+S and save it.

You should see the total in B5. If a number sits on the left of its cell, Excel is treating it as text. Retype it without spaces or letters. Free alternatives: Google Sheets and LibreOffice Calc use the same formulas.

Power-user layer
  • Every formula starts with =.
  • Excel recalculates by itself when numbers change.
  • Keep data tidy: one table, headers in the top row, no blank rows or columns inside it.
  • Keep raw data and summaries clear and separate.
  • Press Ctrl+S often.
  • Before you start, write on paper the question your numbers should answer. It keeps the sheet simple.
Check yourself: What character must every formula start with?

Answer: The equals sign (=).

slides.title: Why Advanced Spreadsheets?
slides.content:
1. Use formulas to calculate automatically.
  2. Create charts to visualize data.
  3. Examples: Track payments, show spending trends.
📊 Recap: Review Week 3 basics (cells, SUM); show Excel.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Open Excel with a blank workbook.
  2. In A1 type Month, in B1 type Payment.
  3. Type Jan, Feb, Mar in A2:A4 and 50, 60, 70 in B2:B4.
  4. In B5 type =SUM(B2:B4) and press Enter. You should see 180.
  5. Change B3 to 100. The total changes to 220 without you touching the formula.
  6. Select A1:B4. Click Insert, then a column chart.

The formula and chart update when the numbers change. If the total does not change, click Formulas, then Calculation Options, and choose Automatic.

Power-user layer
  • Never type totals by hand. Use formulas so the sheet stays correct when numbers change.
  • Select any cells and look at the bottom bar of Excel. It shows the Sum, Average and Count at once.
  • Save a clean copy as a template, then use Save As for each new month.
  • Learn in this order: SUM, IF, VLOOKUP, charts, sort, filter. Pivot tables come later.
  • Keep a backup copy of important files.
Check yourself: Why use =SUM instead of adding on a calculator?

Answer: The sum updates by itself when numbers change, and it avoids typing mistakes.

slides.title: Reviewing Excel Basics
slides.content:
1. Cells: Boxes for data (e.g., A1).
  2. Rows/Columns: Horizontal/vertical lines.
  3. SUM: Adds numbers (e.g., =SUM(B1:B3)).
  4. Open Excel: Start → Type “Excel” → Click.
⭐ Activity: Open Excel and review your tracker file.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Click Start, type Excel, press Enter. Choose Blank workbook, or File, Open to find your tracker.
  2. Click cell A1. Look at the Name Box at the top-left. It shows A1.
  3. Type Item, press Tab, type Cost, press Enter.
  4. Fill B2:B4 with numbers.
  5. Click B5, type =SUM(B2:B4), press Enter. (Or select B2:B4 and press the AutoSum button, the Σ on the Home tab.)

You should see the total. If you see ##### the column is too narrow. Double-click the line between the column letters to widen it.

Power-user layer
KeysWhat it does
Ctrl+ArrowJump to edge of data
Ctrl+HomeGo to A1
F2Edit a cell
Alt+=AutoSum
Ctrl+ZUndo
Ctrl+SSave

In B1:B3 the colon means "from B1 to B3". Press Esc to cancel a cell edit.

Check yourself: What does =SUM(B1:B3) add up?

Answer: The values in B1, B2 and B3, the whole range from B1 to B3.

slides.title: Using the IF Formula
slides.content:
1. IF Formula: Checks conditions (e.g., “Is budget over $100?”).
  2. Step 1: Type expenses in B1:B3 (e.g., $50, $120, $80).
  3. Step 2: In C1, type =IF(B1>100,"High","Low").
  4. Step 3: Press Enter; copy to C2:C3.
⭐ Activity: Use the IF formula to label expenses as “High” or “Low.”
Step-by-step layer
  1. Type 50, 120, 80 in B1:B3.
  2. Click C1 and type =IF(B1>100,"High","Low"). Use straight quote marks.
  3. Press Enter. C1 shows Low.
  4. Click C1. Drag the small square at its bottom-right corner down to C3. (Double-clicking that square also works.)

You should see Low, High, Low. The formula says: if B1 is more than 100, write High, otherwise write Low.

If you see #NAME?, check spelling and quotes. If Excel complains about the formula, your region may need semicolons instead of commas. LibreOffice and Google Sheets use the same IF.

Power-user layer
  • The pattern is IF(test, result if true, result if false).
  • Tests use >, <, >=, <=, = and <>.
  • Put the limit in a cell, say E1, and write =IF(B1>$E$1,"High","Low"). Press F4 to add the dollar signs. Now you change one cell to change all results.
  • Ctrl+D fills a formula down.
  • Always test the exact limit value.
Check yourself: With =IF(B1>100,"High","Low"), what appears if B1 is exactly 100?

Answer: Low. 100 is not greater than 100.

slides.title: Using VLOOKUP
slides.content:
1. VLOOKUP: Finds data in a table (e.g., item prices).
  2. Step 1: Create a price list (e.g., A1:A2 = “Milk,” “Bread”; B1:B2 = $2, $3).
  3. Step 2: In D1, type =VLOOKUP("Milk",A1:B2,2,FALSE).
  4. Step 3: Press Enter (shows $2).
⭐ Activity: Use VLOOKUP to find specific data in your spreadsheet.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Type Milk in A1, Bread in A2, 2 in B1 and 3 in B2.
  2. Click D1 and type =VLOOKUP("Milk",A1:B2,2,FALSE).
  3. Press Enter. You should see 2.
  4. Change "Milk" to "Bread". The answer becomes 3.

Read it like this: look for Milk in the first column of A1:B2, give me the value from column 2, and match exactly (FALSE).

If you see #N/A, the word was not found. Check spelling and extra spaces. Also check that the thing you search for is in the first column of the table.

Power-user layer
  • Use FALSE for an exact match.
  • VLOOKUP only looks to the right of the first column.
  • Press F4 on the table range to lock it ($A$1:$B$2) before you copy the formula down.
  • Wrap it to show friendly text: =IFERROR(VLOOKUP(...),"Not found").
  • In recent Microsoft 365 versions, XLOOKUP is also available and easier. Check your version.
  • Keep price lists in one place and look them up, rather than retyping prices.
Check yourself: In =VLOOKUP("Milk",A1:B2,2,FALSE), what does the 2 mean?

Answer: Return the value from the second column of the table range, which is the price column.

slides.title: Creating a Chart
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Enter data (e.g., months in A1:A3, expenses in B1:B3).
  2. Step 2: Highlight data (A1:B3).
  3. Step 3: Click Insert → Column Chart.
  4. Step 4: Add title (e.g., “Monthly Expenses”).
⭐ Activity: Create a chart in Excel.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Type Jan, Feb, Mar in A1:A3 and amounts in B1:B3.
  2. Select A1:B3 by dragging.
  3. Click the Insert tab.
  4. In the Charts group, click Insert Column or Bar Chart and choose Clustered Column.
  5. Click the words "Chart Title" on the chart and type Monthly Expenses.

You should see one column for each month. Chart empty or odd? Click it, press Delete, and select the data again including the labels. Use the plus button beside the chart to add data labels. In LibreOffice use Insert, Chart. In Google Sheets use Insert, Chart.

Power-user layer
  • Alt+F1 makes a chart right away from selected data.
  • Insert, Recommended Charts suggests a good type for you.
  • Use columns to compare, lines for change over time, and a pie only for a few parts of one whole.
  • Always add a title and label the axes. Avoid 3-D effects.
  • To use a chart in Word or PowerPoint, click it, press Ctrl+C, and paste with Ctrl+V.
Check yourself: Which chart type suits spending over several months, and why?

Answer: A line chart or column chart. A line shows the trend over time clearly.

slides.title: Sorting Data
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Enter items and prices (e.g., A1:A3, B1:B3).
  2. Step 2: Highlight data (A1:B3).
  3. Step 3: Click Data → Sort → Sort by Price (High to Low).
⭐ Activity: Sort a list in Excel.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Put headers Item and Price in row 1. Add three items below.
  2. Select all the data including headers.
  3. Click Data, then Sort.
  4. Tick My data has headers. For Sort by choose Price. For Order choose Largest to Smallest.
  5. Click OK.

You should see the rows rearranged, with each item still beside its own price. If the names and prices get mixed up, press Ctrl+Z at once. This happens when only one column was selected. In Google Sheets use Data, Sort range.

Power-user layer
  • Click any cell inside a tidy table and press the A to Z or Z to A button on the Data tab. Excel selects the whole table.
  • Use Add Level to sort by two things, such as Category then Price.
  • Blank rows break a table. Remove them.
  • Numbers stored as text sort wrongly. Convert them first.
  • Save a copy before sorting a large sheet.
  • Check formulas after sorting.
Check yourself: Why must you select all the columns before sorting?

Answer: So each row moves as a whole. If you sort only one column, items and prices become mismatched.

slides.title: Filtering Data
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Add headers (e.g., “Item,” “Price”).
  2. Step 2: Click Data → Filter.
  3. Step 3: Click dropdown in Price; select “Greater than $10.”
⭐ Activity: Use filters to hide irrelevant data in your spreadsheet.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Put headers Item and Price in row 1 with data below.
  2. Click any cell in the table.
  3. Click Data, then Filter. Small arrows appear in the header cells.
  4. Click the arrow beside Price. Choose Number Filters, then Greater Than.
  5. Type 10 and click OK.

You should see only rows with prices above 10. Other rows are hidden, not deleted. The row numbers turn blue. To clear, click the arrow and choose Clear Filter. If nothing works, check there is a header row and that the prices are real numbers, not text.

Power-user layer
  • Ctrl+Shift+L switches filters on and off.
  • Inside the filter arrow, untick items you do not want. Use the search box for long lists.
  • The bottom-left of Excel shows how many records were found.
  • To total only the visible rows, use =SUBTOTAL(109,B2:B20).
  • Clear filters before you share the file, so no one thinks data is missing.
Check yourself: Does a filter delete the rows that do not match?

Answer: No. It only hides them. Clear the filter to show them again.

slides.title: Creating a Payment Schedule
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Label A1:B1 as “Month,” “Payment.”
  2. Step 2: Enter months (e.g., Jan, Feb in A2:A4).
  3. Step 3: Enter payments (e.g., $50, $60, $70 in B2:B4).
  4. Step 4: Use SUM in B5; create a chart.
📅 Guide: Build a payment schedule together.
Step-by-step layer
  1. In A1 type Month, in B1 type Payment.
  2. Type Jan in A2. Drag its bottom-right corner down to A4. Excel fills Feb and Mar.
  3. Type 50, 60, 70 in B2:B4.
  4. In A5 type Total. In B5 type =SUM(B2:B4). You should see 180.
  5. Select A1:B4. Click Insert, choose a column chart, and give it a title.

If the total misses a month, click B5. Coloured borders show which cells are included. Fix the range. Format money by selecting B2:B5 and pressing Ctrl+1, then choose Currency.

Power-user layer
  • Add a Paid column and a Balance column, with =B2-C2 for the balance.
  • Use real dates and the Date format, so sorting works by time.
  • Freeze the header row: View, Freeze Panes, Freeze Top Row.
  • Press Ctrl+T to turn the range into a Table, so formulas and charts grow with new rows.
  • Conditional formatting (Home tab) can colour late payments.
Check yourself: Which formula totals the payments in B2:B4?

Answer: =SUM(B2:B4)

slides.title: Saving and Reviewing
slides.content:
1. Save: Click File → Save As → “My Files 2025” → “My Schedule.”
  2. Check: Review formulas and chart for errors.
  3. Reopen: Open File Explorer, double-click file.
⭐ Activity: Save and reopen your file.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Press Ctrl+S. In recent versions, click Browse if shown. (F12 opens Save As directly.)
  2. Go to the folder My Files 2025.
  3. In File name type My Schedule. Keep the type as Excel Workbook. Click Save.
  4. Check the title bar shows My Schedule. Close Excel.
  5. Press Windows+E to open File Explorer. Go to My Files 2025 and double-click the file.

You should see your data and chart again. Review: click cells with formulas, look for errors such as #### or #N/A, and check the total with a calculator. Cannot find the file? Use File, Open, Recent in Excel.

Power-user layer
  • Ctrl+S often. F12 saves a new copy under a new name.
  • Press Ctrl+` (the key above Tab) to show all formulas. Press it again to go back.
  • Name files clearly with dates, like My_Schedule_2025-03.xlsx. Avoid "final2".
  • Keep a second copy on a flash disk or cloud storage.
  • If Excel closes without saving, open Excel and look under File, Open, Recent, or File, Info, Manage Workbook for recovery.
Check yourself: How do you reopen your file when Excel is closed?

Answer: Open File Explorer (Windows+E), go to the My Files 2025 folder, and double-click the file.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Create a payment schedule (3 months, payments).
  2. Task 2: Use SUM to calculate total.
  3. Task 3: Create a column chart.
  4. Task 4: Save as “My Schedule” in “My Files 2025.”
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!
Step-by-step layer
  1. Open a blank workbook. In A1 type Month and in B1 Payment. Add Jan, Feb, Mar and 50, 60, 70.
  2. In A5 type Total. In B5 type =SUM(B2:B4). You should get 180.
  3. Select A1:B4. Click Insert, then Clustered Column. Title it Payment Schedule.
  4. Press F12, choose My Files 2025, name it My Schedule, click Save.

Expected result: a table, total of 180, a chart with three columns, and a saved file. Stretch challenge: add column C with =IF(B2>55,"High","Low") filled down, then filter to show only High.

Power-user layer
  • Use this checklist: headers, data, formula, chart, saved.
  • Test your formula by changing one number. The total must change.
  • Practise until you can do it with few mouse clicks: Tab, Enter, Alt+=, Alt+F1, Ctrl+S.
  • Look at your chart and ask whether a stranger would understand it.
  • Save a backup before experimenting.
Check yourself: You change B3 from 60 to 100. What should the total be now if the others are 50 and 70?

Answer: 220, because 50 + 100 + 70 = 220. If it does not change, check the formula.

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Analyze budgets or schedules.
  2. Visualize data with charts.
  3. Prepare for presentations next week!
⏳ Note: Advanced spreadsheets help in real life.
Step-by-step layer

Build a tracker for something real.

  1. Choose a need: shop sales, savings group (chama) contributions, or school fees.
  2. Make headers: Date, Item, Amount.
  3. Enter at least five rows of real or practice data.
  4. At the bottom, add a total with =SUM(...).
  5. Select the data and insert a column chart.
  6. Press Ctrl+S and name the file clearly.

You should see a tidy table, an automatic total and a chart. Slip: typing the total by hand. Always use a formula, so that it changes when the numbers change.

Power-user layer
  • Spreadsheets are used in administration, sales, accounts, data entry, shop keeping and reports for projects.
  • A clear chart in a report helps a manager decide quickly.
  • Good habits: clear headers, one kind of data per column, no merged cells inside data, and regular backups.
  • Accurate records help with loans, tax records and proposals.
  • Employers value people who can tidy and explain numbers.
Check yourself: Name one spreadsheet you could build to help a small business.

Answer: A daily sales and expenses tracker with totals, or a stock list where VLOOKUP finds prices. Any realistic example is correct.

slides.title: Q&A and Homework
slides.content:
1. Ask: Any questions about Excel?
  2. Homework:
    1. Create a payment schedule with 4 entries.
    2. Add a SUM formula and a chart.
    3. Save and reopen the file.
  3. Next Week: Creating presentations!
❓ Encourage: Ask questions and use handouts for practice.
Step-by-step layer

Common beginner questions:

  1. My formula shows as text, not a result. The cell may be formatted as Text. On the Home tab set Number Format to General, then retype the formula.
  2. What are the #### signs? The column is too narrow. Double-click the column border.
  3. Must I buy Excel? No. Google Sheets and LibreOffice Calc are free and use the same formulas.
  4. How do I undo a mistake? Press Ctrl+Z.

Homework tip: save, close and reopen, to be sure the file is safe.

Power-user layer
  • Do the homework with real numbers from your life.
  • Check the total with a calculator once, to build trust in your formula.
  • Press Ctrl+` to view all formulas and check them.
  • Name the file clearly and keep a copy.
  • Write down errors you meet. Error messages are clues, not failures.
Check yourself: A VLOOKUP shows #N/A. Name two likely causes.

Answer: The word searched for is not found, perhaps through a spelling mistake or extra spaces, or it is not in the first column of the table.

slides.title: Creating Presentations
slides.content:
1. Objective: Learn to make and share slide presentations.
  2. Today: Use PowerPoint to create slides.
  3. Why It Matters: Share ideas clearly (e.g., plans, hobbies)!
  4. What would you like to present? (e.g., a trip plan)
Step-by-step layer

Before you open anything, decide what one thing your audience should remember. Example: a 3-slide plan for a chama trip to Naivasha.

  1. Write the goal in one sentence: "We travel on 14 December and each member pays KES 3,000."
  2. Split it into three ideas: where, when, cost.
  3. Open PowerPoint (or Google Slides) and choose Blank Presentation.
  4. You should see one slide with a Title box and a Subtitle box, and a slide pane on the left.

Common slip: starting by choosing fancy designs. Plan the words first, then decorate.

Power-user layer

Good presenters plan on paper first. One slide, one idea. If you cannot say a slide's point in one sentence, split it. Slides support your voice; they are not a script to read aloud. Think of your audience: a chama wants dates and amounts, a church committee wants a clear request. Ask yourself, "What should they do after this?" and end with that. Next learn layouts and consistent themes, because they save the most time.

Check yourself: Why write your goal in one sentence before opening PowerPoint?

Answer: It tells you what each slide must say and what to leave out, so the deck stays short and focused instead of becoming a pile of random text.

slides.title: What Is Microsoft PowerPoint?
slides.content:
1. A program to create slides for presentations.
  2. Examples: Share a travel plan, show a budget.
  3. Alternative: Google Slides (works in a browser).
⭐ Activity: Open PowerPoint or Google Slides on your computer.
Step-by-step layer

PowerPoint is a program for building slides; Google Slides does the same in a browser and saves automatically to your Google account. Try both quickly:

  1. PowerPoint: Start, type "PowerPoint", press Enter, click Blank Presentation.
  2. Google Slides: open Chrome, go to slides.google.com, sign in, click Blank presentation.
  3. You should see a slide in the middle and a thumbnail list on the left in both.
  4. Click the title box and type "Test".

Common slip: Slides needs internet to open at first. If it will not load, check your connection or data bundle. LibreOffice Impress is a free offline option.

Power-user layer

The three differ in where files live. PowerPoint files (.pptx) sit on your computer unless you save them to OneDrive. Google Slides lives online and can export to .pptx. Impress opens .pptx too, but fancy animations and fonts may shift. If you must present on someone else's computer, bring a PDF copy as a backup. Pick the tool your audience can open. Next learn to share and co-edit the same deck online.

Check yourself: You will present on a venue computer with no internet. Which format is the safest backup, and why?

Answer: A PDF copy (or the .pptx on a flash drive), because it opens without internet or your account and keeps the layout fixed.

slides.title: Opening Microsoft PowerPoint
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click Start (Windows icon, bottom-left).
  2. Step 2: Type “PowerPoint” in the search bar.
  3. Step 3: Click Microsoft PowerPoint to open.
⭐ Activity: Open PowerPoint on your own computer.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Click the Start button (Windows icon, bottom-left).
  2. Type PowerPoint. Windows searches while you type.
  3. Click Microsoft PowerPoint in the results (or press Enter).
  4. On the start screen, click Blank Presentation.

What you should see: a window with a ribbon (tabs such as Home, Insert, Design) across the top and one empty slide. Right-click the PowerPoint icon on the taskbar and choose Pin to taskbar, so next time it is one click.

Common slip: it is not found. It may not be installed; use Google Slides in Chrome instead.

Power-user layer

Pin the programs you use daily to the taskbar to avoid searching. On the start screen, the Recent list shows files you worked on lately, so you rarely need to hunt through folders. The Windows key then typing works from anywhere. Sign in with a Microsoft account if you want autosave to OneDrive. If the screen shows "Product Activation Failed" or a trial banner, the licence needs sorting; free alternatives exist. Next, learn the ribbon layout.

Check yourself: A learner types PowerPoint in the Start search and nothing appears. Give two possible reasons or fixes.

Answer: It may not be installed on that computer, or the spelling is wrong. Check the spelling, then use Google Slides or LibreOffice Impress as a free alternative.

slides.title: Understanding PowerPoint
slides.content:
1. Slides: Pages in your presentation.
  2. Slide Pane: Left side shows all slides.
  3. Toolbar: Top has tools (e.g., text, images).
⭐ Activity: Find and name the slide pane and toolbar in PowerPoint.
Step-by-step layer

Open a blank presentation and identify the parts:

  1. Slide pane (left): small thumbnails, one per slide. Click one to open it.
  2. Slide area (centre): where you type and place pictures.
  3. Ribbon (top): tabs Home, Insert, Design, Transitions, Slide Show. Click Insert and watch the buttons change.
  4. Notes (bottom): click "Click to add notes" to write what you will say.
  5. Status bar (very bottom): shows the slide number and the zoom slider.

Common slip: the slide pane vanished. Click View, then Normal to restore it.

Power-user layer

Experts rarely hunt through menus. The Tell Me or Search box at the top of the ribbon (Alt+Q in current Microsoft 365) finds any command by name. Learn the quick access toolbar for Save and Undo (Ctrl+Z). Slide Sorter view (View tab) lets you drag slides into a new order. If the ribbon is hidden, double-click any tab to pin it back. Learn the names of the parts, because help articles and tutors use them.

Check yourself: Your slide thumbnails on the left have disappeared. How do you get them back?

Answer: Click the View tab and choose Normal view, which shows the slide pane again.

slides.title: Creating a New Slide
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open PowerPoint (blank presentation).
  2. Step 2: Click Home → New Slide.
  3. Step 3: Choose a layout (e.g., Title and Content).
⭐ Activity: Add a slide to your presentation.
Step-by-step layer

Example: build slide 2 of a business pitch.

  1. In the slide pane, click the slide after which the new one should appear.
  2. Click Home, then the New Slide button (click the lower arrow to see layouts).
  3. Choose Title and Content.
  4. Click the title box and type "Our Prices"; click the content box and type your list.

You should see the new thumbnail appear below the selected one. Shortcut: Ctrl+M adds a new slide.

Common slip: clicking the main part of the button gives the same layout as the last slide. Use the arrow to pick a different layout.

Power-user layer

Layouts give you placeholders that keep spacing and fonts consistent. Avoid drawing your own text boxes when a layout has a placeholder: placeholders feed the Outline view and screen readers. Changed your mind? Home, then Layout, converts an existing slide without losing text. Use Duplicate Slide (right-click the thumbnail) to copy a slide you like. Drag thumbnails to reorder. A clean deck uses only a few layouts. Learn Slide Master next to change all slides at once.

Check yourself: You added a slide but its layout is wrong. How do you change it without retyping?

Answer: Select the slide, click Home, then Layout, and pick the layout you want; your text moves into the new placeholders.

slides.title: Adding Text to a Slide
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click in the title box; type (e.g., “My Travel Plan”).
  2. Step 2: Click in the content box; type (e.g., “Visit Paris”).
  3. Step 3: Format text (e.g., Bold, 20pt font).
⭐ Activity: Type a title and text on a slide.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Click the title box and type "My Travel Plan".
  2. Click the content box and type three lines, pressing Enter after each: Mombasa, Diani, Lamu.
  3. Select the text with the mouse. On Home, set size 28 and click Bold (Ctrl+B).
  4. Press Tab at the start of a line to make a sub-bullet; Shift+Tab to undo it.

You should see bullets, with the title larger than the body. Click outside the box to finish.

Common slip: text overflows. Keep to about six lines of a few words each, or split into two slides.

Power-user layer

The rule experts follow: big, short, and few. Use at least about 24 point for body text so people at the back can read. Use one or two fonts across the whole deck. High contrast (dark text on light background, or the reverse) beats clever colours. Write phrases, not sentences. If PowerPoint shrinks your text automatically (AutoFit), that is a sign you have too much on the slide. Learn to use Format Painter to copy styling.

Check yourself: Your content box has twelve long lines and the text became tiny. What should you do?

Answer: Split the content over two or more slides and shorten each line to a phrase, instead of letting AutoFit shrink the text.

slides.title: Inserting an Image
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click Insert → Pictures.
  2. Step 2: Choose an image from “My Files 2025” (e.g., a photo).
  3. Step 3: Resize by dragging corners.
⭐ Activity: Insert and resize an image in your slide.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Click the slide where the picture should go.
  2. Click Insert, then Pictures, then This Device.
  3. Browse to your folder, click the photo, then Insert.
  4. Drag a corner handle (not a side handle) to resize; this keeps the shape proportional.
  5. Drag the picture to the spot you want.

You should see small circles around the picture when selected. Right-click, then Edit Alt Text, to describe it for people using screen readers.

Common slip: dragging a side handle stretches the photo. Press Ctrl+Z and use a corner.

Power-user layer

Phone photos can be several megabytes each, which makes a deck slow to email on mobile data. Select a picture, open Picture Format, then Compress Pictures to shrink them. Crop (also in Picture Format) instead of squashing. Use photos you own or have permission to use; a picture found online may be copyrighted. Keep text legible over images by placing it on a plain area. Learn to group and align objects next.

Check yourself: You resize a photo by dragging the middle of its right edge and it looks stretched. Why, and what is the fix?

Answer: Side handles change only the width. Undo, then drag a corner handle to resize proportionally.

slides.title: Using Templates
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click Design → Themes.
  2. Step 2: Choose a theme (e.g., colorful background).
  3. Step 3: Apply to all slides for consistency.
⭐ Activity: Apply a theme to your presentation.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Click the Design tab.
  2. In the Themes group, hover over a theme; the slide previews it live.
  3. Click one to apply it to every slide.
  4. In the Variants group, pick a colour variation if you want.

You should see all thumbnails change at once. To apply a theme to only some slides, right-click the theme and choose Apply to Selected Slides.

Common slip: choosing a dark, busy design that makes text hard to read. If you cannot read it from a metre away, change it.

Power-user layer

A theme is a bundle of fonts, colours and layouts, which is why changing it restyles everything consistently. Do not mix several themes in one deck; consistency looks professional. Keep a plain background for printed handouts to save ink. Check your business's colours and logo: put the logo on the Slide Master (View, Slide Master) once, and it appears on every slide. Design Ideas, if your version shows it, suggests layouts for a slide, but review them.

Check yourself: Why apply one theme to all slides instead of a different one per slide?

Answer: A single theme keeps fonts, colours and layout consistent, which looks professional and is easier for the audience to follow.

slides.title: Creating a 3-Slide Presentation
slides.content:
1. Slide 1: Title (e.g., “My Summer Plan”).
  2. Slide 2: List 3 items (e.g., places to visit).
  3. Slide 3: Add an image and a sentence.
🗂️ Guide: Build a short presentation together.
Step-by-step layer

Worked answer for the "My Summer Plan" deck:

  1. Slide 1, Title Slide layout: title "My Summer Plan", subtitle your name.
  2. Ctrl+M for a new Title and Content slide. Title "Places to Visit"; bullets: Mombasa, Naivasha, Kisumu.
  3. Ctrl+M again. Title "Why Mombasa". Type one sentence, then Insert, Pictures to add a photo.
  4. Design tab: apply one theme.
  5. Press Ctrl+S and save.

Stretch challenge: add a fourth slide with a table of costs in KES (Insert, Table) and a total.

Power-user layer

Notice the structure: opening, content, one memorable closing slide. That pattern works for school talks, chama updates and sales pitches. Build the full skeleton first, then polish; people who perfect slide 1 run out of time. Use the Notes pane for your speaking points. Rehearse aloud once: if a slide takes more than about two minutes, it carries too much. Next, learn Slide Show timing and handouts.

Check yourself: In the 3-slide plan, what should slide 3 contain, and what is a common mistake with it?

Answer: One image and one sentence that sums up your message. The common mistake is overloading it with paragraphs or several pictures.

slides.title: Saving and Presenting
slides.content:
1. Save: Click File → Save As → “My Files 2025” → “My Presentation.”
  2. Present: Click Slide Show → From Beginning.
  3. Navigate: Click or press arrow keys to move slides.
⭐ Activity: Save and present your slides.
Step-by-step layer

Save first, then present.

  1. File, then Save As, then Browse. Choose your folder (for example "My Files 2025").
  2. Type the name "My Presentation" and click Save. After that, Ctrl+S saves updates.
  3. Click the Slide Show tab, then From Beginning (or press F5).
  4. Press the Right Arrow, Space or click to advance; Left Arrow goes back.
  5. Press Esc to leave.

You should see the slide fill the screen with no ribbon. Common slip: starting with From Current Slide (Shift+F5) and missing the first slides.

Power-user layer

Save early and often; a power cut in the middle of work is common. Use Save As, then PDF if you want a copy others cannot accidentally change. In Slide Show, press B for a black screen when you want attention back on you, and press a number plus Enter to jump to a slide. Presenter View (Slide Show tab) shows your notes privately when a second screen or projector is connected. Always run through the deck once on the actual projector before the event.

Check yourself: What is the difference between starting a show From Beginning and From Current Slide?

Answer: From Beginning (F5) starts at slide 1; From Current Slide (Shift+F5) starts at the slide you have selected, so earlier slides are skipped.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Create a 3-slide presentation.
  2. Task 2: Add a title, text, and an image.
  3. Task 3: Apply a theme.
  4. Task 4: Save as “My Presentation” and present it.
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!
Step-by-step layer

Full worked answer:

  1. Open PowerPoint, click Blank Presentation.
  2. Slide 1: type a title "My Hobby: Football" and your name in the subtitle.
  3. Ctrl+M. Add title "What I Do" and three bullets.
  4. Ctrl+M. Insert, Pictures, This Device, pick a photo, and resize from a corner.
  5. Design tab: click a theme.
  6. File, Save As, name "My Presentation", Save.
  7. Press F5 and click through; press Esc at the end.

Check: three slides, one picture, same theme on each. Stretch challenge: add speaker notes to every slide and export a PDF.

Power-user layer

If anything fails, work out which step broke before restarting. Picture missing? You may have clicked Online Pictures instead of This Device. Theme only on one slide? It was applied to selected slides. Experts check their own work against a short list: spelling, readable size, consistent theme, saved file. Run the spell checker (F7). Ask a friend to view it for thirty seconds and tell you what they remember; that reveals whether the message works.

Check yourself: After the task, how can you quickly check your deck is ready to present?

Answer: Confirm there are three slides, text and a picture are present, one theme is applied, spelling is checked (F7), the file is saved, and F5 plays it from the start.

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Share ideas (e.g., travel plans, hobbies).
  2. Present information clearly.
  3. Prepare for virtual meetings next week!
⏳ Note: Presentations help in real life.
Step-by-step layer

Presentations are how ideas get shared in school, church, business and online meetings. Practise with a real use: a one-slide shop offer.

  1. New slide, Title Only layout.
  2. Title: "Maize Flour 2 kg offer".
  3. Insert, Text Box, type the offer and your phone number.
  4. Insert a photo and save.
  5. Next week you will share a slide like this on Zoom.

What you should see: a clean, readable slide you could show a customer. Common slip: too many words; cut to what matters.

Power-user layer

Presenting clearly is a transferable skill. Whoever explains plainly wins trust in a meeting, a loan pitch or a school committee. Practise by presenting to one person and asking what stayed with them. Start with one key message, three supporting points, and a call to action. Over time learn charts (Insert, Chart) to turn numbers into pictures. Be ready for next week: you will share your slides in a Zoom call.

Check yourself: Name three parts of a clear short presentation.

Answer: A single key message, a few supporting points, and a call to action or closing line telling the audience what to do next.

slides.title: Q&A and Homework
slides.content:
1. Ask: Any questions about PowerPoint?
  2. Homework:
    1. Create a 3-slide presentation about a hobby.
    2. Add text, an image, and a theme.
    3. Save and practice presenting.
  3. Next Week: Virtual meetings with Zoom!
❓ Encourage: Ask questions and use handouts for practice.
Step-by-step layer

Possible questions, with answers:

  • Can I use PowerPoint without internet? Yes, the installed app works offline; Google Slides needs setup for offline use.
  • My file will not open on another PC. Save as PDF, or check the other PC has a compatible app.
  • How many slides should I make? Enough for your time, about one per one to two minutes.
  • Homework steps: pick a hobby, make three slides, add a picture and theme, save, practise with F5.
Power-user layer

Homework tips: write your three slide titles on paper before opening the program. Time yourself when presenting: about one minute per slide. Say it out loud to a mirror or friend. Keep your saved file in a named folder so you find it next week. If stuck, write down the exact message or step where you got stuck; precise questions get quick help. Next week the deck will be shared in Zoom.

Check yourself: Your deck will not open on a friend's computer. Name two ways to get around it.

Answer: Save a PDF copy for them to open, or upload to Google Slides or Drive and share a link.

slides.title: Virtual Meetings
slides.content:
1. Objective: Learn to use Zoom for online meetings.
  2. Today: Join, manage, and share in Zoom meetings.
  3. Why It Matters: Connect with friends or groups remotely!
  4. Who would you like to meet online? (e.g., family)
Step-by-step layer

Virtual meetings let people see and hear each other over the internet. Try the flow in miniature:

  1. Check you have a working internet connection (open any website).
  2. Check headphones or speakers are plugged in.
  3. Decide who you will meet and when, for example a family call on Sunday at 4 pm.

You will need: a device with a camera and microphone (laptop or phone), and either the Zoom app or a browser. Common slip: waiting until the minute of the meeting to test. Test ahead.

Power-user layer

Online meetings use data. Video uses much more than audio only, so on a limited bundle, turn the camera off and join by audio when video is not needed. Use a quiet spot with light in front of you rather than behind. Keep your device charged or plugged in. Use whichever tool the other people use (Zoom, Google Meet, Teams); the skills transfer. Next learn the controls and etiquette.

Check yourself: You have a small data bundle and a long meeting. How can you reduce data use?

Answer: Turn your camera off, mute when not speaking, and close other apps that use the internet.

slides.title: What Is Zoom?
slides.content:
1. A program for video calls and meetings.
  2. Examples: Chat with family, discuss plans.
  3. Free to use for basic features.
🖥️ Show: Display Zoom on a projector; explain as a video phone.
Step-by-step layer

Zoom is an app (and website) for video meetings. The host starts a meeting and gets a Meeting ID and a link; others join with either.

  1. Open Chrome and go to zoom.us.
  2. Look for Join (for guests) and Sign In (for people with accounts).
  3. Note that you can join without an account in most cases.

You should see a Join page asking for a meeting ID. Basic features are free. Common slip: confusing "Host a Meeting" with "Join"; as a guest, you only need Join.

Power-user layer

Meeting hosts control settings such as waiting room and passcode; participants cannot change them. Only click meeting links from people you know; fake invites are used by scammers. Never share the link of a private meeting on public social media. Zoom is just one tool; Google Meet and Teams work in a similar way. Free plans may have limits on meeting length or size, so check what is current before planning an important meeting.

Check yourself: What is the difference between a host and a participant?

Answer: The host creates and controls the meeting (settings, admitting people, ending it); a participant joins using the ID or link.

slides.title: Opening Zoom
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click Start (Windows icon, bottom-left).
  2. Step 2: Type “Zoom” in the search bar.
  3. Step 3: Click Zoom to open.
  4. Alternative: Open Chrome, go to zoom.us, click “Join a Meeting.”
🖱️ Demo: Show how to open Zoom; help learners as needed.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Click Start and type Zoom.
  2. Click Zoom Workplace (or Zoom) in the results.
  3. The window shows Join and Sign In buttons.

No app? Use the browser instead: open Chrome, go to zoom.us/join, type the meeting ID, click Join, then choose "Join from your browser" if offered.

You should see a dialog asking for the meeting ID. Common slip: the link opens the browser but nothing happens; allow the pop-up for opening Zoom, or pick browser join.

Power-user layer

The app has the most features, and the browser version covers the basics. If installing is blocked on a shared computer, browser join saves you. Keep Chrome updated, since old browsers have trouble with video. The first time, Chrome asks permission for the microphone and camera; click Allow. If you click Block by mistake, click the padlock beside the address, and change it. Learn to sign in later so your name appears correctly.

Check yourself: Chrome asked to use your camera and you clicked Block. How can you fix it?

Answer: Click the padlock or settings icon beside the web address, change Camera and Microphone to Allow, and reload the page.

slides.title: Joining a Zoom Meeting
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Get a meeting ID (e.g., from an email).
  2. Step 2: Open Zoom, click “Join.”
  3. Step 3: Enter meeting ID and your name.
  4. Step 4: Click “Join Meeting.”
🔗 Practice: Join a test meeting with a sample ID.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Copy the meeting ID (about nine to eleven digits) and passcode from the email or message.
  2. Open Zoom and click Join.
  3. Enter the meeting ID, then your name (for example "Wanjiru Mwangi") and click Join.
  4. Enter the passcode if asked.
  5. Choose Join with Computer Audio, and wait if you see "Waiting for the host".

You should see the video gallery. Common slip: typing the ID with spaces or a wrong digit gives "Invalid meeting ID". Paste it from the message instead.

Power-user layer

If the invitation has a link, clicking it is easier than typing the ID. Use your real name so the host recognises you and lets you in from the waiting room. Join a few minutes early to check sound. If you cannot hear, check the speaker choice by clicking the arrow beside the microphone icon. If the meeting is "not started", the host has not arrived; wait rather than retrying again and again. Do not share a private link with outsiders.

Check yourself: Zoom says "Invalid meeting ID". What are two things to check?

Answer: Check you typed the digits exactly (best to copy and paste), and that the meeting was not ended or scheduled for a different time.

slides.title: Using Zoom Controls
slides.content:
1. Mute/Unmute: Turn microphone off/on.
  2. Video On/Off: Show/hide your camera.
  3. Participants: See who’s in the meeting.
  4. Leave: Click to exit the meeting.
🎛️ Show: Controls in a real Zoom meeting.
Step-by-step layer

The bottom toolbar holds the main controls:

  1. Mute/Unmute: click the microphone. A red slash means you are muted.
  2. Start/Stop Video: click the camera icon.
  3. Participants: see the list and use Raise Hand.
  4. Chat: type a message to everyone or one person.
  5. Leave: click the red Leave button, then confirm.

Shortcuts on Windows: Alt+A for mute and unmute, Alt+V for video. If the toolbar disappears, move the mouse. Common slip: talking while muted; check the red slash.

Power-user layer

Hold the Space bar to talk temporarily while muted, then release. Ask a question quietly with Chat rather than interrupting. The arrow beside the microphone and camera opens audio and video settings, where you can pick devices. The host can ask to "unmute" you but cannot do it without your consent, so you will see a prompt. Leave, rather than closing the laptop lid, so you do not appear to hang in the meeting. Learn Raise Hand for large meetings.

Check yourself: You are speaking but nobody responds. What is the first thing to check?

Answer: Whether the microphone icon has a red slash, meaning you are muted. Click it to unmute, and check the correct microphone is selected.

slides.title: Sharing Your Screen
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Join a Zoom meeting.
  2. Step 2: Click “Share Screen.”
  3. Step 3: Choose a window (e.g., PowerPoint from Week 7).
  4. Step 4: Click “Share.”
🖥️ Practice: Share a Week 7 presentation.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Join a meeting.
  2. Open your PowerPoint file first, so it is ready.
  3. Click the green Share Screen button on the toolbar.
  4. Pick the PowerPoint window (not "Desktop") and click Share.
  5. In PowerPoint, press F5 or choose Slide Show; others see your slides.
  6. Click Stop Share (red) at the top when done.

You should see a green border around the shared window. Common slip: sharing the whole desktop, which also shows your notifications and other windows.

Power-user layer

Share one window rather than your whole screen to protect private things (WhatsApp, banking, emails). Turn on Do Not Disturb to hide notification popups. To play a video with sound, tick Share Sound before sharing. If participants cannot see changes, check you are not sharing a different window. In presenting, run the slide show in a window, so you can still see the Zoom controls. The host may restrict who can share; ask them to allow it.

Check yourself: Why choose a single window instead of Desktop when sharing?

Answer: It prevents others seeing private items like notifications, chats or other open files, and keeps the audience focused on the one window.

slides.title: Scheduling a Meeting
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Zoom, click “Schedule.”
  2. Step 2: Set date, time, and topic (e.g., “Family Chat”).
  3. Step 3: Copy meeting ID and link.
  4. Step 4: Email the link (use Gmail from Week 4).
📅 Show: Schedule a meeting and copy the link.
Step-by-step layer
  1. In Zoom, click Schedule.
  2. Type the topic "Family Chat", pick the date and start time, and check the time zone (Nairobi is East Africa Time).
  3. Keep the passcode setting on.
  4. Click Save. Zoom may open your calendar.
  5. Click Copy Invitation and paste it into an email or WhatsApp message.

You should see the meeting in your Meetings tab with Start and Copy Invitation. Common slip: wrong AM/PM; read the time back before saving.

Power-user layer

Include in the invitation: topic, date, time with time zone, link, and passcode. Send it a day ahead and again an hour before. If people are in different countries, state the time in each place, since mix-ups here are very common. You can edit a scheduled meeting from the Meetings tab if plans change, and the same link stays valid. Do not post the link publicly if it is a private meeting. Next, practise starting the meeting as host.

Check yourself: What details should an invitation include so people can join without confusion?

Answer: The topic, date, time with time zone, the meeting link or ID, and the passcode.

slides.title: Testing Your Audio and Video
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Join a test meeting (e.g., zoom.us/test).
  2. Step 2: Test microphone (speak, check sound bars).
  3. Step 3: Test video (turn on camera, check image).
🎤 Practice: Run a test meeting in class.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Go to zoom.us/test in Chrome and click Join.
  2. Click Open Zoom Meetings if asked; allow camera and microphone.
  3. When you see the screen "Can you hear a ringtone?", click Yes. Repeat for "speak and pause".
  4. Check your face appears in the video box.
  5. Click Join with Computer Audio.

You should see sound bars move as you speak. Common slip: wrong microphone chosen. Click the arrow beside the mic icon and choose another device, such as your headset.

Power-user layer

Test with the same headset and place you will use in the real meeting. Headphones prevent echo, because speakers feed back into the microphone. Face a window rather than having light behind you. Check what is visible in your background. Keep the laptop plugged in. If your sound is crackly, close other programs and move closer to the router or switch from Wi-Fi to cable if you can. Doing this ten minutes early saves embarrassment.

Check yourself: Others hear an echo when you talk. What is the most likely cause and fix?

Answer: Your speakers are feeding back into your microphone. Use headphones or lower the speaker volume.

slides.title: Etiquette for Zoom Meetings
slides.content:
1. Mute: Turn off microphone when not speaking.
  2. Background: Choose a tidy or virtual background.
  3. Focus: Avoid distractions during meetings.
🤝 Discuss: Polite Zoom behavior.
Step-by-step layer

Meeting manners in practice:

  1. Join early, with your name shown correctly.
  2. Mute until you speak; use Raise Hand to ask.
  3. Choose a tidy place or blur your background: click the arrow beside Video, then Video Settings or Backgrounds.
  4. Look at the camera, not just the screen, when speaking.
  5. Close other tabs and silence your phone.

Common slip: forgetting you are unmuted and having private conversations heard.

Power-user layer

Etiquette is trust: show up, listen, be brief. Dress as you would for an in-person version of the meeting. If you must leave, say so in the chat. Do not record or screenshot others without their consent. Keep side comments in chat professional, since the host can save the chat. In a crowded home, headphones with a mic, and a polite "I'm on a call" sign, help. Practise being concise: one point at a time.

Check yourself: Give two etiquette rules that improve a meeting for everyone.

Answer: Stay muted when not speaking and avoid distractions or side talk; also join on time and use the Raise Hand or chat to speak in turn.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Join a test Zoom meeting.
  2. Task 2: Practice mute/unmute and video on/off.
  3. Task 3: Share a PowerPoint slide from Week 7.
  4. Task 4: Schedule a meeting and copy the link.
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!
Step-by-step layer

Worked answer:

  1. Task 1: go to zoom.us/test and join.
  2. Task 2: click the mic icon to mute and again to unmute (Alt+A). Click the camera icon to turn video off and on (Alt+V). Confirm icons change.
  3. Task 3: open your PowerPoint file, then Share Screen, pick the PowerPoint window, Share, and press F5.
  4. Task 4: Schedule, topic "Practice", pick a time, Save, Copy Invitation, paste it in a message to yourself.

Stretch challenge: schedule a real meeting for a friend and ask them to join; watch them in Participants.

Power-user layer

Check yourself: could you do each task without the notes? Write down the three steps you are least sure of. Pros keep a checklist before every meeting: audio, video, shared file open, invitation sent. If screen sharing shows a black window, close and reopen the shared program, or share the Desktop briefly. Take note of any error text you get, because it points to the fix. Next week you will store files online.

Check yourself: During Task 3, others see a black screen instead of your slides. What can you try?

Answer: Stop sharing, make sure the PowerPoint window is open and not minimised, then share again; if it still fails, share the whole Desktop for a moment.

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Connect with friends or family online.
  2. Share ideas in meetings.
  3. Prepare for cloud storage next week!
⏳ Note: Virtual meetings help in real life.
Step-by-step layer

Online meetings let you do business and family matters without travelling. Example use: a group-savings meeting of 8 members.

  1. Schedule it and copy the invitation.
  2. Send it in the group chat the day before.
  3. Share the agenda slide on screen at the start.
  4. Next week: store the files in Google Drive so everyone can open them.

You should see members join in the Participants list. Common slip: sending the link at the last minute.

Power-user layer

Meetings save transport costs and time, but only if well run. A good meeting has a clear purpose, a start time, a time limit and a note of decisions afterwards. Send the agenda in advance, and send a short summary of decisions after. Many people now work with clients across towns or countries using these skills. Next you will learn cloud storage, which is where shared documents live.

Check yourself: List two things to do before and one after a meeting.

Answer: Before: schedule and send the invitation and agenda. After: send a short summary of the decisions and next steps.

slides.title: Q&A and Homework
slides.content:
1. Ask: Any questions about Zoom?
  2. Homework:
    1. Join a test Zoom meeting (use zoom.us/test).
    2. Share a file or slide in a meeting.
    3. Schedule a meeting and email the link.
  3. Next Week: Cloud storage with Google Drive!
❓ Encourage: Ask questions and use handouts for practice.
Step-by-step layer

Likely questions:

  • Do I need an account to join? Usually not; you need the ID or link.
  • Can I join from my phone? Yes, install the Zoom app and tap Join.
  • Why is my video frozen? Weak connection; turn video off or move closer to the router.
  • Is it safe? Use passcodes, do not share links publicly, and accept only known people from the waiting room.
Power-user layer

Homework tips: do the test meeting at a different time of day and note whether quality changes. When sharing a file, open it before you click Share. When scheduling, send the invitation to a real person and ask them to confirm they could join. Write down any trouble and what fixed it, such as "mic needed Allow in Chrome". That personal troubleshooting note becomes a valuable guide.

Check yourself: A friend says "I clicked the link and nothing happened". Give two things for them to try.

Answer: Allow the browser to open Zoom or choose "Join from your browser", and check they have the correct, complete link and a working internet connection.

slides.title: Cloud Storage and Collaboration
slides.content:
1. Objective: Learn to save and share files online.
  2. Today: Use Google Drive to store and collaborate.
  3. Why It Matters: Access files anywhere, share safely!
  4. What files would you like to store? (e.g., photos)
Step-by-step layer

Cloud storage keeps files on the internet instead of only one device. Use it for a real need: your CV.

  1. Open Chrome and go to drive.google.com.
  2. Sign in.
  3. Upload your CV (New, File upload).
  4. Open it from your phone later, with the same sign-in, to see it is there.

You should see the file in My Drive on both devices. Common slip: signing in to a different Google account on the second device and thinking the file is lost.

Power-user layer

Cloud storage is not the same as a backup in every case: if you delete a file from Drive, it goes to Trash and is removed after a while, and sync can copy mistakes everywhere. Keep important documents in two places. Use a strong password and turn on two-step verification on your Google account, since it protects everything stored. Never share your password. Next learn folders and sharing settings.

Check yourself: You cannot find your file on your phone, but it was on your laptop. What is the first thing to check?

Answer: Whether you are signed in to the same Google account on both devices.

slides.title: What Is Google Drive?
slides.content:
1. A free online storage service for files.
  2. Examples: Save photos, documents, or presentations.
  3. Access from any computer or phone with internet.
🗄️ Explain: Drive is a digital filing cabinet; show Drive.
Step-by-step layer

Google Drive gives free space tied to a Google account (see what is currently offered on the Drive site). Practise finding your space:

  1. Go to drive.google.com and sign in.
  2. Look at the bottom-left for the storage bar.
  3. Click New and notice you can upload files or create Docs, Sheets and Slides.
  4. Open a Google Doc, type a line and note it saves automatically.

You should see "Saved to Drive" near the title. Common slip: filling the space with large videos; delete what you do not need and empty Trash.

Power-user layer

Google Docs, Sheets and Slides made inside Drive usually count differently from uploaded files, so check Google's current rules. Free storage is shared across Gmail and Photos, so a full mailbox can block uploads. Use Drive for the mobile app too, to scan documents with your phone camera. Sensitive documents such as ID copies need care: do not share them as "anyone with the link". Learn to search Drive by file type and name.

Check yourself: Drive says storage is full. Name two ways to free space.

Answer: Delete large files you no longer need and empty the Trash; also check that Gmail and Photos are not using the space.

slides.title: Accessing Google Drive
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Google Chrome.
  2. Step 2: Go to drive.google.com.
  3. Step 3: Sign in with your Gmail account (from Week 4).
🌐 Demo: Show how to open Drive; help learners as needed.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Open Chrome and go to drive.google.com.
  2. If you see Go to Drive, click it; otherwise click Sign in.
  3. Type your Gmail address, click Next, type the password, and click Next.
  4. You should see "My Drive" and your files (empty if new).

Tip: bookmark the page. In Chrome press Ctrl+D.

Common slip: "Wrong password". Click "Forgot password?" and follow the recovery steps. On a shared computer, always sign out after, and use an Incognito window if possible.

Power-user layer

Do not sign in on public computers without signing out afterwards; click your profile picture, then Sign out. Turn on two-step verification so a stolen password is not enough. Never click links in messages that claim "your Drive is full, sign in" without checking the address begins with drive.google.com or accounts.google.com. You can switch between accounts using the profile picture. Know your recovery phone number or email.

Check yourself: Why should you sign out of Drive on a cybercafe computer?

Answer: Otherwise the next person using the machine could open your files and email. Sign out and close the browser window.

slides.title: Understanding Google Drive
slides.content:
1. My Drive: Where your files are stored.
  2. New Button: Add files or folders.
  3. Shared with Me: Files others share with you.
📁 Show: Point to key areas in a real Drive interface.
Step-by-step layer

Learn the main areas of Drive's left menu:

  1. New: button at the top left to upload or create things.
  2. My Drive: files you own. Click to open folders.
  3. Shared with me: files others gave you access to.
  4. Recent and Starred: quick returns; right-click a file and choose Add to Starred.
  5. Trash: deleted items.

You should see each area change the file list. The grid or list icon at top right switches the view. Common slip: a shared file is not in My Drive; look in Shared with me, and use Add shortcut to My Drive if you want it there.

Power-user layer

My Drive means you own it; Shared with me means someone else owns it and could remove your access. Make a copy (right-click, Make a copy) if you need to keep it permanently. Search at the top supports names, owners and file type. Sort by Last modified to find what you changed. Items in Trash are not gone yet, so you can recover mistakes quickly. Learn the difference between ownership and access, which matters when someone leaves a group.

Check yourself: Your friend shared a file but you cannot see it in My Drive. Where is it?

Answer: In "Shared with me". You can add a shortcut to My Drive if you want it there.

slides.title: Uploading a File
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click “New” → “File upload.”
  2. Step 2: Choose a file from “My Files 2025” (e.g., “My Presentation”).
  3. Step 3: Click “Open” to upload.
⬆️ Practice: Upload a Week 7 presentation.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Click New, then File upload.
  2. In the window, browse to "My Files 2025" and click "My Presentation".
  3. Click Open. A small box at the bottom right shows progress.
  4. When done, you see a green tick and the file in My Drive.

Quick option: drag the file from the folder into the Drive browser tab. You can select many files with Ctrl+click.

Common slip: closing the tab before the upload completes. On a slow connection, wait for the green tick.

Power-user layer

Large files take time and data. Check the file size before uploading on a mobile bundle. Uploading a folder works too: New, Folder upload. If you upload a .pptx, you can open it in Google Slides with right-click, Open with. Keep clear names, like "CV_Wanjiru_2025.pdf" rather than "final final 2". Uploading creates a copy; changing the original later does not update the Drive copy unless you use Drive for desktop. Learn that sync tool later.

Check yourself: You edited "My Presentation" on your laptop after uploading it. Why does Drive still show the old version?

Answer: An upload is a copy made at that moment; changes to the original are not sent unless you upload again or use a sync tool.

slides.title: Creating a Folder
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click “New” → “Folder.”
  2. Step 2: Name it (e.g., “Photos 2025”).
  3. Step 3: Upload files into the folder.
🗂️ Practice: Create a folder and organize files.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Click New, then Folder.
  2. Type "Photos 2025" and click Create.
  3. Double-click the folder to open it.
  4. Click New, File upload, and choose a photo; or drag files in.
  5. To move an existing file: right-click it, choose Move, pick the folder, click Move.

You should see the file when you open the folder. Common slip: files left loose in My Drive. Use Move to tidy.

Example structure: Business, then 2025, then Receipts.

Power-user layer

Folders work like cabinets: choose names you will still understand in a year. Use dates in a consistent format (2025-03) so sorting works. A shared folder shares everything inside it, including files added later, which is handy for a team but be careful with private files. Right-click a folder and change its colour for quick recognition. Use shortcuts, not copies, to place one file in two folders. Next learn sharing permissions.

Check yourself: You share a folder with a friend. What happens to files you add to it later?

Answer: They become accessible to your friend as well, since sharing applies to everything in the folder.

slides.title: Sharing a File
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Right-click a file (e.g., “My Presentation”).
  2. Step 2: Click “Share” → Add email address.
  3. Step 3: Choose “View only” or “Can edit.”
  4. Step 4: Click “Send” to share via Gmail.
🔗 Practice: Share a file with view-only access.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Right-click "My Presentation" and click Share.
  2. In "Add people and groups" type the email address.
  3. Click the role box and choose Viewer (view only), Commenter or Editor (can edit).
  4. Tick Notify people and add a short message.
  5. Click Send.

You should see the person's name in the list with the role. Common slip: choosing Editor when Viewer was enough. Change it any time in Share.

To undo access, open Share and set the person's role to Remove access.

Power-user layer

Give the minimum access needed: Viewer for most. Under General access, "Anyone with the link" is convenient but means anyone who gets the link can open it, so never use it for private papers like ID copies, payslips or financial records. Restricted means only listed people. Check who has access from time to time, and remove people when a project ends. Viewers can still download a file unless you turn that off in the settings.

Check yourself: When is "Anyone with the link" a poor choice?

Answer: When the file is private or sensitive, because anyone who obtains the link, even by forwarding, can open it. Use Restricted and list specific people.

slides.title: Collaborating on a File
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Share a file with “Can edit” access.
  2. Step 2: Open file (e.g., Google Docs in Drive).
  3. Step 3: Edit together in real-time.
👥 Demo: Real-time editing with a test file.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Share a Google Doc with a friend as Editor.
  2. Both open it at the same time.
  3. Type a line; the friend's cursor appears with their name in colour.
  4. To suggest instead of editing, click the pencil icon (top right) and choose Suggesting.
  5. Select text, press Ctrl+Alt+M to add a comment.

You should see changes appear within seconds. Common slip: two people editing the same sentence. Agree who edits which section, or use comments.

Power-user layer

Version history (File, Version history, See version history) shows who changed what and lets you restore an older version, so mistakes are recoverable. Use Suggesting mode for proofreading so the owner approves changes. Name versions at important milestones. Type @name in a comment to notify someone. Only people with Editor access can change the content; Commenters can only comment. Large Excel uploads do not co-edit unless opened as Google Sheets.

Check yourself: Someone accidentally deleted a paragraph in a shared Doc. How can you recover it?

Answer: Open File, Version history, See version history, and restore the earlier version, or copy the paragraph back from it.

slides.title: Downloading a File
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Right-click a file in Google Drive.
  2. Step 2: Click “Download.”
  3. Step 3: Save to “My Files 2025” folder.
⬇️ Practice: Download a file from Drive.
Step-by-step layer
  1. Right-click a file in Drive.
  2. Click Download.
  3. If Chrome asks, choose "My Files 2025" and click Save (otherwise it goes to Downloads).
  4. Open the folder and check the file is there.

For a Google Doc, Download offers formats like Word (.docx) and PDF. In an open Doc use File, Download.

Common slip: not knowing where it went. In Chrome press Ctrl+J to see downloads, and click "Show in folder".

Power-user layer

Downloading makes a separate copy; edits to it will not change the Drive version. Choose PDF to share a fixed document, or .docx if the receiver needs to edit. Downloading many files makes a zip file; right-click, Extract All to open it. Download files from people you trust only, and scan unknown attachments, as they can carry viruses. Free up space on small devices by moving finished files to Drive after you download backups.

Check yourself: You downloaded a file but cannot find it. What shortcut helps in Chrome?

Answer: Press Ctrl+J to open the Downloads list, then click Show in folder.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Upload a file to Google Drive (e.g., “My Presentation”).
  2. Task 2: Create a folder “Photos 2025” and move a file into it.
  3. Task 3: Share a file with view-only access.
  4. Task 4: Download a file to “My Files 2025.”
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!
Step-by-step layer

Worked answer:

  1. Task 1: New, File upload, pick "My Presentation", Open. Wait for the green tick.
  2. Task 2: New, Folder, name "Photos 2025", Create. Right-click a file, Move, choose the folder, Move here.
  3. Task 3: right-click a file, Share, enter a friend's email, set Viewer, Send.
  4. Task 4: right-click, Download, save to your folder, and confirm.

Check: the file is inside the folder and your friend can open it. Stretch challenge: create a shared folder "Group Project", add two members as Editors, and upload a file into it.

Power-user layer

If a friend cannot open your link, check the email was typed correctly and that you pressed Send (not Cancel). If it says "You need access", the request goes to you in your email. Keep one master folder structure, and review sharing monthly. Experts work from a short checklist: right folder, right name, right permission. Next week you will learn about PDFs, a format that is easy to share and not easy to change by accident.

Check yourself: Your friend opens your link and sees "You need access". What does it mean and what do you do?

Answer: Their account does not have permission. Add their email in Share with the right role, or change General access if appropriate.

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Store photos, documents safely.
  2. Share files with friends or family.
  3. Prepare for PDFs next week!
